narrative: Markets are navigating crosscurrents between major AI catalysts, persistent central bank hawkishness, and escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. Anthropic's upsized $107.3 billion IPO and Nvidia's quarterly revenue beat provided structural support to tech sentiment, though concerns over compute costs, gross margins, and expanding US chip export curbs remain prevalent. Meanwhile, the S&P 500 fell for five consecutive sessions as hawkish Federal Reserve commentary signaling further rate hikes prompted rotations toward defensive equities and high-quality fixed income. Commodities are under distinct pressures: gold and industrial metals have slumped sharply despite falling Treasury yields, while crude oil faces competing forces from broader demand worries and Middle East supply disruption risks following US strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island.

Nasdaq.why: Sentiment is lifted by Anthropic's landmark $107.3 billion debut and Nvidia's strong earnings outlook, as noted by Ruhell Amin and Mark Cudmore, though Thomas Hayes and Winnie Hsu warn of intermediate tech jitters and capex scrutiny.

S&P 500.why: The index declined for five consecutive sessions, burdened by hawkish Fed policy expectations, regulatory scrutiny in healthcare, and broader rotation out of concentrated high-multiple equities.

Gold.why: Prices dropped below $2,030 per ounce, pressured by expectations of further US interest rate hikes and broader metals liquidations, on track for its worst annual performance since 2013 according to Abeer Abu Omar.

Oil.why: Brent crude faced downward pressure from global demand concerns, but Ziad Daoud highlights severe upside risk from potential supply disruptions following US strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island.

priced_in: Federal Reserve maintaining a higher-for-longer policy path with up to three rate hikes priced in
Anthropic IPO robust demand, valuation at approximately 16 times run-rate revenue, and a first-day pop
Nvidia's strong data center order book and zero anticipated data center revenue from China due to export curbs
Investor rotation out of concentrated tech into defensives and high-quality fixed income
debates: AI build-out durability: Sustained demand and aggressive forward guidance versus gross margin compression and capex sustainability concerns
Driver of the metals collapse: Mark Cudmore questions whether the slump in gold and copper reflects Anthropic IPO liquidity needs, deleveraging, or hidden China demand deterioration
Oil market trajectory: Global economic slowdown weighing on Brent versus geopolitical supply shocks in the Strait of Hormuz flagged by Ziad Daoud
Treasury dynamics: Yield curve shifting lower on flight-to-safety flows despite Fed rhetoric signaling more rate hikes
